entities.name: PMID:25089641
observations: Haji et al., Anesthesiology 2014, studied 27 adults undergoing on-pump coronary artery surgery with simultaneous echocardiography and invasive hemodynamics at five perioperative stages.

entities.name: Fixed septal curvature predicts PCWP
observations: A fixed interatrial septal-curve pattern predicted PCWP >=17 mmHg with AUC 0.89 and PCWP >=18 mmHg with AUC 0.98 in adults undergoing on-pump coronary surgery.
In this study, fixed interatrial septal curvature was the strongest echocardiographic predictor of elevated invasively measured PCWP.

entities.name: Doppler poor after induction
observations: After anesthesia and mechanical ventilation, conventional Doppler variables correlated poorly with PCWP in TTE and TEE; in patients with normal ejection fraction, correlations were poor at all stages.
Pulmonary-vein S/D <1 was only modestly discriminative, with AUC 0.74 for PCWP >=17 mmHg and 0.78 for PCWP >=18 mmHg.

entities.name: Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure
observations: Invasive pulmonary capillary wedge pressure measured simultaneously with echocardiography served as the reference standard in the cardiac-surgery study; the abstract did not specify detailed waveform-validation procedures.
